chinese_source: EXTERNAL epigraphic anchor (non-Chinese): Nalanda copper plate of Devapala, regnal year 39, found 1921 in the antechamber of Monastery 1, Nalanda (Epigraphia Indica XVII)
event: At the request of Balaputradeva, Sailendra king of Suvarnadvipa (Srivijaya), who has built a monastery at Nalanda, Devapala grants five named villages for its monks' requisites, the copying of texts, and the upkeep of the vihara
firmness_reason: A dated royal charter excavated in situ at Nalanda itself; the only uncertainty is Devapala's accession year (c. 810-821 in competing chronologies), which sets the 849-861 window
notes: Endowment rate: five villages for ONE vihara (~30-60 residents) implies roughly 6-12 monks supported per village — the same order as Yijing's implied 15 per village, and a cross-check against Huili's implied 100 per village. Also a Srivijaya synchronism: Balaputradeva's reign must intersect this window.
references: N. G. Majumdar, Epigraphia Indica XVII, The Nalanda Copper-plate of Devapaladeva
